title: Factorization of projective-line chart pushforward through ordinary product exchange
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring, N a natural number annihilating A, and t normalized finite twist transport [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. Let S be any scheme with N invertible in its global sections. Write P = ProjectiveLine(S), q:P → S, W = P ×_S P, and select a projection p_a:W → P by a Boolean a. The opposite projection v_a and p_a give the Cartesian square over q and q. Set L_T = A_T(1)[2]. Define projectionExchange from Rp_a* L_W to q* Rq* L_P by Rp_a* of the inverse normalized line comparison for v_a, followed by inverse ordinary proper exchange [def-sf-p1-integral-transport-data]. Then projectionExchange, followed by ordinaryFiniteP1Exchange for q on L_P, followed by direct image of the normalized line comparison for ProjectiveSpace.map q, equals ordinaryFiniteP1DiagonalChartMap [lem-sp-finite-p1-diagonal-kummer-component-formula]. This equation contains no trace and no splitting family.

proof.text: For each Boolean projection, use the canonical or flipped pullback square. The isoPullback projection identities identify the chart followed by its selected projection with the projective projection, and its opposite projection with ProjectiveSpace.map q.

Transport exact-derived exchange to left-derived exchange by canonical exact/left-derived comparison isomorphisms and the invariance of mates under isomorphism of left adjoints. This identifies ordinaryFiniteP1Exchange with the canonical derivedBaseChangeMap. Prove the chart pasting equation for inverse-image square comparisons using leftDerivedUpperStarComp associativity. Transpose the desired exchange pasting identity under the chart projection adjunction, substitute the composite-adjunction counit, and use naturality and the chart triangle identity. Proper base change supplies the invertible product exchange.

For positive N, uniqueness of normalized finite twist transport identifies t with the canonical finiteEtaleTwistPullbackData transport. Its composition law gives composition of the line comparisons. For N=0, invertibility of zero makes the base scheme empty, and hence the source scheme empty; maps into its Tate-line sheaf are unique. Transport the line composition equation through the degree-zero exact-derived comparison and shift by two, then through the canonical left-derived comparison. All these coherence calculations are proved directly from the singleFunctor and commShift naturality and composition identities.

Expand projectionExchange, substitute the proved exchange pasting identity, and cancel proper exchange with its inverse. Use shifted line composition, naturality of the chart adjunction unit and of the pushforward composition comparison, and cancellation of the inverse line comparison. The remaining morphism is the unit followed by rightDerivedLowerStarCompHom and the chart line comparison. Apply lem-sf-p1-chart-map-composition to identify this with ordinaryFiniteP1DiagonalChartMap. No trace formula or diagonal Kummer component theorem is used.

lean.statement:
theorem chartExchange
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (N : ℕ) (hA : (N : A) = 0) (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤))) (a : Bool) :
    projectionExchange A N hA t S hS a ≫
        ordinaryFiniteP1Exchange A (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S)
          ((ordinaryFiniteLine A N hA (ProjectiveLine S))⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧) ≫
        (ordinaryFinitePushforward A
          (ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine S) ↘ ProjectiveLine S)).map
          (ordinaryFiniteShiftedLinePullback A N hA t
            (ProjectiveSpace.map (ULift.{u} (Fin 2)) (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S))
            (finiteP1_unitOnPullback N (ProjectiveLine S ↘ S) hS)).hom =
      ordinaryFiniteP1DiagonalChartMap A N hA t S hS a
